rich_summary: This passage recounts a pivotal episode in Karna’s life. While his teacher Parashurama (Rama of the Bhrigu line) sleeps with his head on Karna’s lap, a monstrous worm burrows into Karna’s thigh. Karna endures unbearable pain in silence so as not to disturb his guru, demonstrating extraordinary endurance and devotion. The worm turns out to be a cursed Asura freed by Parashurama’s presence. But the blood awakens the sage, who realizes that no Brahmana could endure such agony; suspecting deception, he forces Karna to reveal that he is not a Brahmana but of mixed or lower birth. Angered by the lie used to obtain divine weapons, Parashurama curses Karna so that the Brahma weapon will fail him when he most needs it. The section then shifts to a royal self-choice ceremony where Duryodhana abducts a princess, with Karna fiercely defending him against assembled kings.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces Karna studying weapons under Parashurama, establishing the mentorship that leads to the tragic revelation.
Depicts the horrifying worm biting into Karna’s thigh and the beginning of his silent endurance.
Parashurama realizes Karna cannot be a Brahmana because of his superhuman tolerance for pain—triggering the confrontation.
Parashurama’s curse that the Brahma weapon will fail Karna in a crucial battle—one of the defining tragedies of his destiny.
Transition to the Kalinga princess’s self-choice ceremony where Duryodhana abducts the maiden, beginning the martial display of Karna’s loyalty.

top_scenes.scene_text: Parashurama sleeps peacefully with his head on Karna’s lap while a monstrous bristled worm burrows into Karna’s bleeding thigh and he remains perfectly still in agony.
Parashurama rises in anger after discovering Karna’s deception and pronounces a terrible curse while the trembling warrior kneels before him.
Duryodhana seizes the princess at the Kalinga svayamvara and rides away in his chariot as Karna turns to face a pursuing host of enraged kings.
